Surah 66: At-Tahrim (The Prohibition). It is Medinan, and its verses number twelve.

﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ (seeking) from your slave-woman Mariyah the Copt, when he had intercourse with her in the house of Hafsah, while she was away. She came back, and it grieved her that this happened in her house and on her bed, when you said: "She is forbidden to me." ﴿seeking﴾ by this prohibition ﴿the pleasure of your wives﴾, that is, their approval. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — He forgave you this prohibition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 2:

﴿Allah has certainly ordained﴾ prescribed ﴿for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ its dissolution (taḥlil) by the expiation (kaffārah) mentioned in Surat al-Mā'idah. Among oaths is the prohibition of a slave-woman. And did the Prophet (ﷺ) make expiation? Muqātil said: he freed a slave (raqabah) regarding the prohibition of Mariyah. And al-Ḥasan said: he did not make expiation, because the Prophet (ﷺ) was forgiven. ﴿And Allah is your Protector (mawlākum)﴾ your Helper.

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when the Prophet confided to one of his wives﴾, she being Hafsah, ﴿a statement﴾, which was the prohibition of Mariyah, and he said to her, "Do not disclose it." ﴿So when she informed [someone] of it﴾, namely Aishah, thinking that there was no harm in that, ﴿and Allah made it known﴾, informed him [the Prophet], ﴿about it﴾, about what was reported, ﴿he made known part of it﴾ to Hafsah, ﴿and overlooked part of it﴾ out of his generosity. ﴿So when he informed her of it, she said, "Who told you this?" He said, "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me"﴾, meaning Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 4:

﴿If you two turn to Allah in repentance, then indeed your hearts have inclined﴾ — that is, Hafsa and Aisha — ﴿toward Allah﴾, meaning they inclined toward the prohibition of Mariya; that is, it pleased you both despite the Prophet's ﷺ dislike of it, and that is a sin. The response to the condition is omitted, meaning: [your repentance will be] accepted. He used the dual "hearts" (qulub) for two hearts and did not express it in the dual (qalbayn), because of the disliking of combining two duals in what is like a single word.

﴿And if you two back each other up against him﴾ — with the assimilation of the second tā' in the original into the ẓā' (tazāharā, i.e., tazzāharā); and in another reading without it, tata'āwanā (cooperate) — ﴿against him﴾, that is, the Prophet, in what he dislikes, ﴿then indeed Allah is his protector﴾ (the word "huwa" here is a separator) — his helper ﴿and Jibril and the righteous among the believers﴾, Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both — coordinated with the grammatical position of the subject of "inna" (so that it reads as "Allah is his protector, and Jibril..."), ﴿and the angels after that﴾, after Allah's help and that of those mentioned, ﴿are [his] supporters﴾, helpers and aides to him in supporting him against you two.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 5:

﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you,﴾ i.e., if the Prophet divorces his wives, ﴿that He substitute for him﴾ (read with both the doubled and the single letter, i.e., yubaddila and yubaddilah) ﴿wives better than you﴾. The predicate of ʿasā (it may be) is the clause "that He substitute," and the clause is the answer to the conditional. The substitution did not occur because the condition did not occur. ﴿Muslims﴾ (muslimāt), those who affirm Islam; ﴿believers﴾ (mu'mināt), sincere; ﴿devout﴾ (qānitāt), obedient; ﴿penitent, worshipping, travelling﴾ (tā'ibāt ʿābidāt sā'iḥāt), fasting, or emigrants (muhājirāt).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 6:

﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families﴾ by driving them toward obedience to God, ﴿from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ — the disbelievers, and stones such as their idols made of them. That is, it is extremely hot, blazing with what has been mentioned, not like the fire of this world, which blazes with firewood and the like. ﴿Over it are angels﴾ its guardians, ﴿their number is nineteen﴾, as will come in "al-Muddaththir". ﴿Harsh﴾ in heart, ﴿severe﴾ in seizing [the damned]. ﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them﴾ — a substitution for "God" (badal min al-jalala), meaning they do not disobey the command of God. ﴿And they do what they are commanded﴾ — an emphasis (ta'kid). The verse is a warning to believers against apostasy (irtidad), and to the hypocrites who profess belief with their tongues without their hearts.

﴿O you who disbelieve, do not make excuses today﴾: this is said to them when they enter the Fire, meaning: because it will not benefit you. ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾: meaning, its recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 8:

﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance.﴾ Read with a fatḥah or a ḍammah on the nūn: sincere, meaning that one does not return to the sin and does not intend to return to it. ﴿Perhaps your Lord will remit from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens﴾ (basātīn) ﴿beneath which rivers flow, on a Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet﴾ (by casting him into the Fire) ﴿and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them﴾ (in front of them) ﴿and [on] their right hands﴾ (will be) ﴿they will say﴾ (this is a new, independent clause) ﴿"Our Lord, perfect for us our light"﴾ (until we reach Paradise), while the hypocrites' light will be extinguished. ﴿And forgive us, our Lord.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*, the "Commentary of the Two Jalals")

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 10:

﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them﴾ i.e., they betrayed them in the religion, since they disbelieved. The wife of Noah, whose name was Wahilah, would say of his people: "He is a madman." And the wife of Lot, whose name was Wa'ilah, would point out his guests to his people when they came to him at night by kindling a fire, and by day by means of smoke. ﴿So they did not avail them﴾ i.e., Noah and Lot, ﴿against God in anything﴾ against His punishment. ﴿And it was said﴾ i.e., it was said to them, ﴿"Enter the Fire along with those who enter"﴾ from among the disbelievers of the people of Noah and the people of Lot.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 11:

﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh.﴾ She believed in Musa, and her name was Asiya. Pharaoh tortured her by driving stakes into her hands and feet, and he placed a great millstone on her chest and exposed her to the sun. Whenever those assigned to her withdrew from her, the angels would shade her. ﴿When she said﴾ during the torture: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾. So it was uncovered for her and she saw it, and the torture became easy for her. ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾ and his torture. ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾, the people of his religion. Then Allah took her soul. Ibn Kaysan said: she was raised to Paradise alive, and so she eats and drinks.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 66, verse 12:

﴿And Mary⦆ is coordinated with "the wife of Pharaoh," ﴿daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity⦆, i.e., preserved it. ﴿So We breathed into it of Our spirit⦆, i.e., Jibril (Gabriel), when he blew into the opening of her garment by God the Exalted's creation, so that it reached her womb, and she conceived Jesus. ﴿And she affirmed the words of her Lord⦆, His laws, ﴿and His books⦆, i.e., His revealed books. ﴿And she was of the devoutly obedient⦆, of the obedient people.
